Subject: Quick clarification on hosted rate-card units (chat vs responses vs legacy)

- For streaming responses, are intermediate tokens billed as they are emitted or only the final assembled output?
- When we use function-calling (returning structured JSON), do function args + returned object count as output tokens or is there a different treatment?
- How do legacy endpoints (we have some old scripts calling /v1/complete) map to the new rate-card — are they still billed differently?
- Do prefix/KV cache hits reduce billed tokens on subsequent calls, or are they charged every time?

Procurement also asked for the baseline hosted list price and a sample invoice line that shows the unit name (so they can reconcile with their internal BE numbers). From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick clarification on hosted rate-card units (chat vs responses vs legacy)

Samir — thanks, and great to hear NeonRetail is moving fast. Attaching the hosted ratecard CSV and a draft SOW for the pilot. Below is a concise mapping and answers to each question so procurement has something they can include in the SOW.

High-level mapping (hosted API billing):
- /responses (new unified endpoint): billed in "response-units" which count total input tokens + output tokens for the call. This is the default for structured outputs and streaming.
- /chat/completions: billed in "chat-units" which are functionally equivalent to response-units for most customers; difference is only in model-specific price points (model X chat SKU vs model X responses SKU).
- legacy endpoints (/v1/complete and older): mapped to the closest new SKU at the time of migration — we bill them under their mapped new SKU on invoices. Legacy calls do not get preferential treatment and are subject to the same token accounting rules once mapped.

Token accounting specifics:
- Streaming: tokens emitted during a stream are billed in the same way as non-streaming responses — we bill for emitted output tokens plus the input prompt tokens. There is no separate "stream surcharge."
- Function calling: both the tokens in the function call arguments and the tokens in the returned structured object are counted as output tokens. If you pass a large JSON payload as arguments, those bytes are included in input token counts.
- Prefix/KV cache: cache hits reduce the billed input tokens only when the request uses the cached prefix and the cache was a hit on our side — subsequent requests that hit prefix cache will show reduced billed tokens on the invoice. Important: a cache miss on the first warm call will bill full tokens.

Discounts and commits:
- Standard pilot/commit brackets: 5% for 3-month pilots (minimum $10k/mo), 12% for 6 months, 18% for 12 months. We can be flexible for strategic customers.
- The discount applies to the hosted SKU list price on invoices after SKU selection and before any tax.

What I'm attaching:
- ratecard-hosted-2027.csv (CSV) — list prices by model & endpoint SKU
- NeonRetail_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft) — pilot scope and milestones

Next steps: if that mapping works, happy to send a small example invoice snippet showing a combined "responses/chat" line and apply a 10% pilot discount for a 3-month commit (we'd treat it as a one-off credit schedule in the SOW). Want to sync today or tomorrow for procurement?

Thanks,
